provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The mechanism is direct. Full-length divider lines of colour palette[3] split the visible grid into a table of cells. The emitted program finds every row and every column that consists only of the line colour. The runs between those lines give the cell-row and cell-column intervals. It works with uneven spacing, rectangular grids and cells only 1 pixel wide.

Cells that are in neither the first/last cell-row nor the first/last cell-column are filled with palette[7]. Each of the four visible corner cells gets a constant colour. The factory computes those constants by sending each original corner through the D4 transform: first reverse the rows (c -> 1-c) if d4 >= 4, then rotate clockwise d4%4 times ((r,c) -> (c,1-r) on the unit square). It then assigns palette[2/4/1/8] to the visible corner each original corner lands on.

All other edge cells keep their input background, and the lines are left unchanged. No normalisation wrapper, inverse rotation or colour unpermutation is used.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the constructor's domain: there are 3 to 5 cell-rows and 3 to 5 cell-columns, so the corner cells are distinct and an interior exists. If there were only 1 cell-row or cell-column, the corners would overlap. In that case the program lets later corner fills overwrite earlier ones (TL, then TR, BL, BR), which is not defined by the puzzle. The line colour is taken as the constant palette[3]. Cells are never entirely the line colour in the generator, so line detection is unambiguous. The approved fixtures match the uniform rule; no fixture contradictions or constructor defects were found. The 'emitted stages' (intermediate canvas) mentioned in the rule text are not produced, and only the final grid is returned. Nothing was tested: I have not run the factory or the emitted program.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The solver finds every row and every column that is entirely the line colour (palette[3]) in the visible grid. The runs between those lines become the cell-row and cell-column intervals. Cells with 1 <= i <= nr-2 and 1 <= j <= nc-2 are filled with palette[7]. Each of the four visible corner cells is filled with a constant colour. The factory computes those constants by mapping each original corner (TL=2, TR=4, BL=1, BR=8) through the D4 transform on the unit square: a column mirror c -> 1-c when d4 >= 4, then d4%4 clockwise turns (r,c) -> (c,1-r). Lines and all non-corner edge cells are left unchanged.
evidence: Constructor: widths and heights are each 3-5 entries with values in 1..6. Dividers sit at cumulative offsets, and `if row >= height: break` skips the phantom line past the last section. Lines are therefore never adjacent, and no cell row or column can be entirely colour 3.
Constructor labels depend only on cell indices (wi, hi) relative to 0 and len-1. No hidden latent other than the visible geometry decides the output colours.

With at least 3 cell-rows and 3 cell-columns, the corner cells and interior cells are disjoint. The solver's order (interior first, then corners) therefore cannot clash, and its output equals the constructor's.

The solver's _intervals reproduces the archived interval logic, including the last segment up to n-1. Detection of full-line rows and columns is symmetric under transposition, so odd D4 variants that swap axes are handled natively.

tf matches standard array semantics. The clockwise rotation old (r,c) -> new (c, n-1-r) is correct. The mirror is applied before rotation, which matches the composition order the host checks, consistent with 8000 passing augmented checks across d4 values.

Every demonstration shows all four corner colours and at least one interior cell. The fixed corner, interior and line colours are therefore taught in-episode; this is not an arbitrary lookup that lacks evidence.
No whole-grid untransform or retransform wrapper is used. The program works directly in visible coordinates with specialised colour constants.
Approved fixtures, including the narrow 2-wide and 1-wide columns in pair 3 and the 15x15 test, are consistent with the cell-index rule.
nonblocking_limits: If there were only 1 cell-row or 1 cell-column, corner fills would overwrite each other in a fixed order. The constructor's 3..5 range excludes this case.
The `nr == 0 or nc == 0` early return is an out-of-domain defensive fallback that the constructor never reaches.
Line colour is the constant palette[3] rather than being inferred. This is valid because the colour is fixed across the episode and appears in every demonstration.
The rule text mentions two emitted canvas stages. The program returns only the final grid. This is a presentation difference and does not affect correctness.
required_context_checks: Confirm the host's D4 convention composes the mirror before rotation, matching tf. Passing augmented checks suggest it does, but the prior notes describe the mirror as 'reverse the rows' while the code mirrors columns.
No colour-evidence check applies: e9c9d9a1 is not in require_colour_evidence's task list, and the corner and interior colours appear in every demonstration.

host_review.resolution: Reviewed constructor invariants, visible-coordinate solver, fixture agreement and documented out-of-domain branches. Source hashes match passing audit.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
